title: Thread Spawning and Joining
summary: Spawn OS threads that execute closures and wait for their completion with JoinHandle.
lecture: Rust threads are native 1:1 OS threads created with `thread::spawn`.
Because spawned threads run independently, variables captured by the closure must be moved into the thread using the move keyword.
Calling join on the returned JoinHandle blocks until the thread finishes and yields its return value wrapped in a Result.

example.code:
let h = thread::spawn(move || 42);
let res = h.join().unwrap();
example.caption: Move data into the thread and join to get the result.
